title: Antibabesial treatment protocols against canine babesiosis
species: B. gibsoni and other Babesia spp.
rationale: Narrative review giving practitioners guidelines on treatment protocols for canine babesiosis; eligible under the review include type.

title: Efficacy of azithromycine and compounded atovaquone for treatment of Babesia gibsoni in dogs
rationale: Same study as PMID:28625019 (Kirk, Levy and Crawford, JVIM 2017; title misspelt). Prospective observational treatment study of 42 PCR-positive dogs (mostly subclinical); full text describes one dog with a haemolytic crisis (PCV 29% to 14%) given emergency transfusion plus azithromycin-atovaquone, then PCR-negative; PCR clearance reported for all.

title: Molecular characterisation of Babesia gibsoni infection from a pit-bull terrier pup recently imported into South Africa.
journal: Journal of the South African Veterinary Association
rationale: Pup with anaemia and thrombocytopenia failed diminazene and imidocarb (PCR still positive) then cleared with atovaquone plus azithromycin.

title: Clinical management of babesiosis in dogs with homeopathic Crotalus horridus 200C.
journal: Homeopathy: the journal of the Faculty of Homeopathy
rationale: Comparison of homeopathic Crotalus horridus (13 dogs) with diminazene (20 dogs) in B. gibsoni dogs with listed clinical signs. Clinical scores and parasitaemia improved in both groups.

title: The case of babesiosis in farmed wolf (Canis lupus L).
rationale: Farmed wolf with typical signs treated with antibiotics with a positive result. Brief, but both parts are present.

title: Management of respiratory syndrome associated with a mixed infection of Babesia canis, Babesia gibsoni and Ehrlichia canis in a Great Dane Pup
syndromes: coinfection; haemolytic anaemia; other: respiratory distress
rationale: Pup with mixed Babesia and E. canis infection, respiratory signs and anaemia, treated with babesicidals, antirickettsials and supportive therapy; uneventful recovery.

title: Detection of a large unnamed Babesia piroplasm originally identified in dogs in North Carolina in a dog with no history of travel to that state.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
species: Babesia sp. (North Carolina large piroplasm, PCR)
rationale: One immunosuppressed lymphoma dog with incidental parasitaemia treated with imidocarb twice; PCR stayed positive to 50 weeks (treatment failure). Clinical syndrome is weak but treatment failure cases are eligible.

title: Canine hepatozoonosis and babesiosis, and feline cytauxzoonosis.
journal: The Veterinary clinics of North America. Small animal practice
rationale: Narrative review covering epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment and control of canine babesiosis.

title: Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment of Pet Dog Babesiosis
rationale: Clinic report of pet dogs clinically diagnosed with babesiosis and given aetiological plus symptomatic treatment with good curative effect; signs, drugs and numbers are not given in the abstract, so this is a weak include.

title: Use of a doxycycline-enrofloxacin-metronidazole combination with/without diminazene diaceturate to treat naturally occurring canine babesiosis caused by Babesia gibsoni.
rationale: Retrospective comparison of doxycycline-enrofloxacin-metronidazole with or without diminazene in naturally infected dogs; efficacy 85.7% vs 83.3% and recovery time reported.

title: Dual infection of rabies virus and Babesia canis in a dog: a case report
rationale: One dog with icterus, weakness and suspected cerebral babesiosis that did not respond to treatment and was found post mortem to have rabies. Treatment drugs are not named in the abstract, so this is borderline.

title: Jaundice In Dog Associated With Babesiosis
journal: International Journal for Agro Veterinary and Medical Sciences
rationale: Labrador bitch with jaundice and hyperbilirubinaemia treated; parasites cleared by day 5 and the dog recovered by day 15.

title: Jaundice in dog associated with babesiosis - A case report
rationale: Labrador bitch with jaundice and hyperbilirubinaemia given antibabesial and supportive therapy; negative by day 5 and fully recovered by day 15 (likely the same case as the other jaundice record).

title: Diagnosis and Curat of Tick Paralysis and Babesia gibsoni Infection of the Tibetan Mastiff Canine Induced by Tick Invasion
rationale: Tibetan Mastiff puppy with paralysis, low haemoglobin and B. gibsoni on smear, cured after ivermectin and Xuechongjing within 3 days.

title: Babesia canis rossi infection in a Texas dog.
rationale: Imported puppy with fever, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and azotaemia; responded to imidocarb and PCR was negative 2 weeks later.

title: The therapeutic efficacy of two antibabesial strategies against Babesia gibsoni.
rationale: Naturally infected dogs treated with atovaquone plus azithromycin (17) or clindamycin, diminazene and imidocarb (13). Recovery, relapse and therapy duration are reported, and haematology was recorded.

title: Re-emergence of Babesia conradae and effective treatment of infected dogs with atovaquone and azithromycin.
rationale: Twelve naturally infected dogs, partly randomised placebo-controlled; atovaquone plus azithromycin cleared B. conradae DNA on PCR whereas placebo dogs stayed positive. Presentation is thin (haemolytic anaemia only).

title: Vector-borne diseases--constant challenge for practicing veterinarians: recommendations from the CVBD World Forum.
rationale: CVBD World Forum practice recommendations on prevention and treatment of canine vector-borne diseases, explicitly including babesiosis; included as a guideline-type review whose subject includes treatment, though depth of babesiosis treatment coverage was not verified.

title: Babesia canis and tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) co-infection in a sled dog.
journal: Annals of agricultural and environmental medicine : AAEM
syndromes: cerebral; coinfection; other: clinical signs of babesiosis (not specified)
rationale: Two sled dogs presented with signs of babesiosis and were diagnosed and treated; the first developed neurological signs from concurrent TBE and was alive for serology 3 months later. Weak include: drugs and Babesia-specific outcome are not detailed in the abstract.

title: The in vitro interactions and in vivo efficacy of atovaquone and proguanil against Babesia gibsoni infection in dogs.
rationale: Experimentally infected dogs treated with Malarone; parasitaemia fell with clinical improvement, then all relapsed with M121I mutation; side effects reported.

title: Clinicopathological Findings and Successful Management of Concurrent Infection of Babesiosis and Ehrlichiosis In Dogs
rationale: Reports clinicopathological findings and successful treatment of concurrent babesiosis and ehrlichiosis in dogs; abstract gives few details.

title: Babesia canis vogeli, Ehrlichia canis, and Anaplasma platys infection in a dog.
rationale: Dog with anaemia, thrombocytopenia and hyperbilirubinaemia co-infected with B. vogeli, E. canis and A. platys; recovered on doxycycline and imidocarb.

title: Babesiosis in dogs: A report of two different cases
rationale: Two dogs with fever, anaemia and, in one, oliguria, icterus and thrombocytopenia; both treated with diminazene, one recovered and one died of hepatic damage.

title: Efficacy of Malarone(®) in dogs naturally infected with Babesia gibsoni.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Eight naturally infected dogs given Malarone with or without doxycycline; parasitaemia and anaemia improved, relapses and retreatment reported.

title: In vitro and in vivo safety and efficacy studies of amphotericin B on Babesia gibsoni.
rationale: Experimentally infected dogs given amphotericin B; parasitaemia fell then recurred and BUN and creatinine rose at 1 mg/kg. Largely in vitro, with limited clinical description.

title: Lahore Canine Fever in a Racing Greyhound
journal: Advances in Animal and Veterinary Sciences
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; coinfection; other: haemorrhagic signs
rationale: Greyhound with fever, red urine and haemorrhagic signs, Babesia and Ehrlichia co-infection; clinical and parasitological cure after imidocarb and doxycycline.

title: Clinical Management of Babesiosis in a Dog along with Blood Transfusion
rationale: Doberman with severe anaemia (PCV 10%) given doxycycline and transfusion; haematology improved and dog recovered.

title: Ocorrência de infecção concomitante natural por Ehrlichia sp., Anaplasma sp. E Babesia sp. em cão assistido no hospital veterinário da universidade federal de Uberlândia
journal: Revista Científica Eletrônica de Medicina Veterinária
rationale: Dog with thrombocytopenia and Ehrlichia, Anaplasma and Babesia co-infection treated with doxycycline and imidocarb; normal counts and no parasites at recheck.

title: New Therapeutic Protocol for Canine Babesiosis: A Case Report
journal: Journal of Dairy Veterinary & Animal Research
rationale: One dog with fever, anaemia, thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly treated with a 10-day drug combination; improved from day 4 and recovered.

title: Actualizarea protocolului de diagnostic în babesioza canină
rationale: Review of the diagnostic protocol that also covers therapy management and drug response by Babesia species. Treatment is part of the subject, though the emphasis is on diagnosis.

title: Tick-borne diseases in dogs
rationale: Narrative nursing review updating babesiosis and other canine tick-borne diseases, including limitations of diagnosis and treatment; included as a review whose subject includes treatment of canine babesiosis, though detail was not verified.

title: Successful Treatment of Babesia gibsoni infection in a Splenectomized dog
rationale: Splenectomised pup with persistent anaemia and thrombocytopenia successfully treated.

title: Actualización sobre la piroplasmosis canina
species: B. canis, B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, B. microti-like
rationale: Practitioner review of canine piroplasmosis from aetiology to treatment; treatment is within scope but abstract is brief.

title: Efficacy, safety and tolerance of imidocarb dipropionate versus atovaquone or buparvaquone plus azithromycin used to treat sick dogs naturally infected with the Babesia microti-like piroplasm.
rationale: Randomised trial of three regimens in 59 naturally infected sick dogs with anaemia and thrombocytopenia; clinical, laboratory and PCR outcomes to 360 days, relapses in imidocarb group.

title: THE USE OF LOW DOSES OF IMIDOCARB FOR THE TREATMENT OF BABESIOSIS IN DOGS
journal: Russian Journal of Agricultural and Socio-Economic Sciences
syndromes: icterus; haemolytic anaemia; other: fever, depression, haemoglobinuria
rationale: Russian/English abstract: dogs with depression, fever, icterus and haemoglobinuria treated with reduced-dose imidocarb (0.3 ml/10 kg), found usable in special cases, which implies a treatment outcome; numbers not given.

title: Efficacy of Azithromycin and Compounded Atovaquone for Treatment of Babesia gibsoni in Dogs.
rationale: Prospective observational treatment study of 42 PCR-positive dogs (mostly subclinical); full text describes one dog with a haemolytic crisis (PCV 29% to 14%) given emergency transfusion plus azithromycin-atovaquone, then PCR-negative; PCR clearance reported for all.

title: Diagnosis and management of concurrent Ehrlichiosis and Babesiosis in a dog.
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; aki; coinfection; other: epistaxis and ocular signs
rationale: Rottweiler with Ehrlichia and Babesia, anaemia and raised BUN and creatinine, treated with several drugs; outcome not stated in the abstract.

title: Therapeutic response monitoring in canine babesiosis – case study
rationale: Full text (Romanian): 10-month-old Akita with pale mucosae, low haematocrit and thrombocytopenia after low-dose imidocarb, retreated with clindamycin; qPCR load fell (Ct 29.8 to >40) and general condition was very good at reassessment.

title: Antiprotozoal treatment of canine babesiosis.
species: B. canis, B. rossi, B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, B. conradae, B. vulpes
rationale: Review of antiprotozoal treatment of canine babesiosis, including relapse and carrier state.

title: Effects of low-dose diminazene aceturate injection followed by clindamycin administration for treating canine babesia gibsoni infection
rationale: Large clinical series of acute B. gibsoni dogs treated with diminazene then clindamycin vs none, with relapse rates compared.

title: Mixed Babesia canis and Anaplasma platys phagocytophilum Infection in Dog
syndromes: other: fever, epistaxis, pale mucosae; coinfection
rationale: Dog with fever, anorexia, epistaxis and pale mucosae, B. canis PCR-positive with Anaplasma co-infection, treated with fluids, analgesic and oxytetracycline; collapsed within 24 h.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Canine Babesiosis in Pakistan, A Case Report
journal: Approaches in Poultry Dairy & Veterinary Sciences
rationale: Single bitch with fever, anaemia, brown urine; full recovery after 21 days.

title: Transfusion of canine cryopreserved red blood cells in treatment of babesiosis
rationale: Full text: dogs with acute babesiosis, azotaemia and raised liver enzymes given basic drug treatment with or without cryopreserved red cell transfusion; haematocrit, haemoglobin and biochemistry normalised by day 10 in the transfusion group.

title: Babesiose canina: relato de caso
journal: LA Referencia (Red Federada de Repositorios Institucionales de Publicaciones Científicas)
rationale: Shih-tzu with petechiae and low haematocrit transfused and treated; recovered by 28 days.

title: Therapeutic management of babesiosis in a dog.
rationale: Boxer with anorexia, cough and respiratory distress treated with diminazene then azithromycin; complete recovery.

title: Studi Kasus : Babesiosis Pada Anjing Persilangan
rationale: Single dog with haemoglobinuria and anaemia treated with clindamycin; clinical improvement by 14 days.

title: Ameliorative effects of alpha-lipoic acid and imidocarb dipropionate on clinico-haematological changes induced by experimental Babesia canis vogeli infection in dogs
rationale: 17-page study of dogs experimentally infected with B. canis vogeli and treated with imidocarb and/or alpha-lipoic acid, with clinical signs and haematology (PCV, RBC, Hb) as endpoints per the earlier screen's accessible information.

title: Diagnosis and treatment of canine babesiosis in dogs
journal: Journal of Dairy Veterinary & Animal Research
rationale: Dog with fever, lethargy and haematuria treated; responded.

title: Clindamycin-doxycycline-metronidazole combination therapy in a refractory canine babesiosis case
treatments: atovaquone; azithromycin; diminazene; clindamycin; doxycycline; metronidazole
rationale: Relapsing refractory B. gibsoni after atovaquone-azithromycin; triple therapy cleared parasite with repeated relapses on withdrawal.

title: Malarone® induced pancreatitis and alopecia in a dog: a case report.
species: B. gibsoni (suspected; PCR negative at referral)
rationale: One dog treated with atovaquone-proguanil for suspected B. gibsoni who developed drug-induced pancreatitis and alopecia; adverse-effect report, babesiosis presentation itself not described (low confidence include).

title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE DRUG DIPROCARB FOR BABESIOSIS IN CARNIVORES FROM MOSCOW AND THE MOSCOW REGION
journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
rationale: Field study of imidocarb in naturally infected dogs with symptomatic therapy; claims 100% parasite clearance, clinical detail sparse.

title: Triple Therapy in Canine Babesiosis - A Case Report
journal: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
rationale: Dalmatian with fever, pallor, petechiae and anaemia given triple therapy; recovered with a negative smear by day 10.

title: Therapeutic management and Haemato-biochemical changes of Babesiosis in dogs
journal: Journal of Entomology and Zoology Studies
rationale: Eighteen dogs randomised to imidocarb, oxytetracycline plus doxycycline, or diminazene, with recovery rates and haemato-biochemical normalisation reported.

title: Babesiosis with thrombocytopenia and haemolytic anemia in Dogs: Case study
journal: Journal of Entomology and Zoology Studies
rationale: Dogs with fever, paraplegia, thrombocytopenia and anaemia treated with three drugs; outcome not explicitly stated but drugs and haematology given.

title: Study of efficacy of the drug «Hepatojekt»® in complex therapy of hepatitis in dogs
rationale: Dogs with babesial hepatitis given imidocarb plus Hepatojekt versus basic therapy; metabolic parameters corrected.

title: Novel Granulocytic Colony Stimulating Factor based Therapy for Morbidity Reduction in Pancytopenic Dogs with Babesia gibsoni
rationale: Twenty PCR-positive pancytopenic dogs treated with triple therapy with or without filgrastim; leukocyte rise and better survival reported in the filgrastim group.

title: Successful Therapeutic Management of Babesiosis in a Labrador Dog along with Blood Transfusion
journal: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; icterus; aki; thrombocytopenia; hepatopathy
rationale: Severe anaemia, azotaemia and icterus treated with imidocarb and transfusion; reported as successful.

title: Studi Kasus: Babesiosis (Piroplasmosis) disertai Infestasi Caplak yang Berat pada Anjing Gembala Jerman
rationale: Single German shepherd with anaemia and dehydration treated and improved by day 14.

title: ACHADOS CLÍNICOS E PATOLÓGICOS DE UM CÃO INFECTADO SIMULTANEAMENTE POR Ehrlichia sp., Babesia sp., Hepatozoon sp. E Anaplasma sp.: RELATO DE CASO
rationale: Bitch with Babesia, Ehrlichia, Anaplasma and Hepatozoon, anaemia and thrombocytopenia, treated and markedly improved at 15 days. Drugs are not named in the abstract.

title: EFFICACY OF ANTI-BABESIA DRUGS IN RELATION TO HEMATOLOGICAL PARAMETERS IN DOGS
journal: The Journal of Animal and Plant Sciences
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; other: low pcv, haemoglobin, total protein
rationale: Thirty PCR-confirmed naturally infected dogs with lowered haematology randomised to imidocarb, doxycycline or both; recovery by day 21 (90%, 77%, 62.5%) and pre/post blood values reported.

title: Treatment of Idiopathic Immune Mediated Hemolytic Anaemia in Dogs
rationale: IMHA dogs, 13 secondary to B. gibsoni, treated with immunosuppression plus specific therapy; haematology improved. Babesia subset not separated.

title: An alternative combination therapy with metronidazole, clindamycin and doxycycline for Babesia gibsoni (Asian genotype) in dogs in Hong Kong.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: Retrospective review of 24 dogs failing atovaquone/azithromycin then given triple antibiotic therapy, with PCR clearance rates; clinical syndrome only implicit.

title: Diagnosis and Therapeutic Management of Babesia gibsoni Infection in Dog
journal: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; thrombocytopenia; hepatopathy; aki; other: hypoglycaemia
rationale: Rottweiler with fever, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, raised liver enzymes, BUN and creatinine, treated with imidocarb, fluids, doxycycline and haematinic; clinical recovery within three weeks.

title: Treatment of Secondary Immune Mediated Hemolytic Anaemia of Dogs in Chennai, Tamil Nadu
rationale: Secondary IMHA dogs, 13 of them with B. gibsoni, treated with prednisolone with or without azathioprine plus specific therapy. Hb, PCV, platelets and clinical improvement to day 28 are reported, but the Babesia subgroup is mixed with other causes.

title: A case of Babesia vulpes infection in a dog in Russia.
journal: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
rationale: One dog with severe anaemia and azotaemia treated with imidocarb and atovaquone/azithromycin, euthanised after one week.

title: SPECIFIC CHEMOTHERAPY DRUGS FOR DOGS WITH PYROPLASMOSIS TRANSMITTED BY IXODID TICKS
journal: Scientific and Technical Bulletin оf State Scientific Research Control Institute of Veterinary Medical Products and Fodder Additives аnd Institute of Animal Biology
rationale: Spontaneously infected dogs with anaemia and raised liver and renal values were given two diminazene (Azidine-vet) regimens, one with adjuncts. Haematology and biochemistry at day 7 and 100% efficacy are reported.

title: EVALUATION OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF TREATMENT AND PREVENTION OF DOG BABESIOSIS
rationale: Three groups of five babesiosis dogs given different infusion regimens, comparing clinical recovery and day 1 versus day 10 haematology.

title: Babesiosis in a -3-Month-old Nigerian Indigenous Male Puppy
rationale: 3-month-old puppy with fever, pallor and icterus transfused and given diminazene; fully recovered.

title: An alternative combination therapy with metronidazole and doxycycline for babesiosis and theileriosis in stray dogs
journal: Egyptian Veterinary Medical Society of Parasitology Journal (EVMSPJ)
rationale: Randomised two-regimen trial in stray dogs with Babesia and Theileria; cure rates and haematology reported.

title: Concurrent infection of Hepatozoon canis and Babesia gibsoni in a non-descript dog and its therapeutic management
journal: Journal of Entomology and Zoology Studies
rationale: Dog with fever, icterus, anaemia, thrombocytopenia and raised liver and renal values treated with diminazene, imidocarb and doxycycline; smear negative at one month and uneventful recovery.

title: Tafenoquine Is a Promising Drug Candidate for the Treatment of Babesiosis.
rationale: Tafenoquine given to B. gibsoni-infected splenectomised dogs with parasitaemia, survival, CBC and chemistry monitored (hyperkalaemia noted); mouse and in vitro work accompanies it.

title: Laporan Kasus: Babesiosis pada Anjing Pomeranian
rationale: Single Pomeranian with anaemia, thrombocytopenia and fever treated; improved after 14 days.

title: Emergence of Babesia conradae infection in coyote-hunting Greyhounds in Oklahoma, USA.
rationale: 15 PCR-positive Greyhounds; ill dogs with anorexia, vomiting, fever and anaemia treated with atovaquone/azithromycin, all recovered with negative PCR at 30 and 60 days.

title: Therapeutical Management of Canine Babesiosis in German Shepherd Bitch at Hyderabad, Sindh
rationale: Single bitch with anaemia treated for 21 days and recovered.

title: Co-infection with Babesia canis and Babesia gibsoni in a dog.
treatments: imidocarb; atovaquone; azithromycin; metronidazole; clindamycin; doxycycline
rationale: Dog with lethargy and anaemia; repeated treatment failures and relapse, eventual PCR clearance after metronidazole/clindamycin/doxycycline. Mixed B. canis/B. gibsoni infection.

title: Babesia canis caused clinical babesiosis in a female Shih Tzu dog.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; thrombocytopenia; icterus; other: azotaemia
rationale: Shih Tzu with regenerative anaemia, thrombocytopenia and azotaemia treated with diminazene and others; improved in 4 days, no recurrence at 2 months.

title: Blood Characteristics in Dogs During Treatment of Babesiosis Using Transfusion of Cryopreserved Erythrocytes
rationale: Dogs with babesiosis given cryopreserved erythrocyte transfusion; haematological recovery reported.

title: An atypical case of Babesia bigemina parasitising a dog from a rural area of eastern Mexico.
journal: Revista brasileira de parasitologia veterinaria = Brazilian journal of veterinary parasitology : Orgao Oficial do Colegio Brasileiro de Parasitologia Veterinaria
rationale: Dog with lethargy, fever, pallor and haematuria treated with imidocarb; signs reduced by day 7 and PCR negative day 30.

title: Molecular detection and control of non- regenerative anaemia associated with Babesia gibsoni and Anaplasma platys co- infection in a dog
journal: Journal of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
rationale: Dog with anaemia, thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly; abstract states successful therapeutic management, though drugs are not named.

title: Comparative therapeutic efficacy of imidocarb and diminazene aceturate against Babesia gibsoni in dogs
journal: Journal of Entomology and Zoology Studies
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; icterus; other: fever, epistaxis, melaena
rationale: Twelve clinically ill B. gibsoni dogs randomised to doxycycline-metronidazole plus imidocarb or diminazene; parasitaemia fell by day 15 and smears were negative on day 30.

title: Clinical Efficacy and Safety of Malarone®, Azithromycin and Artesunate Combination for Treatment of Babesia gibsoni in Naturally Infected Dogs.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
rationale: Twelve naturally infected dogs given Malarone, azithromycin and artesunate; haematology normalised and no relapse to 720 days.

title: NON-REGENERATIVE ANAEMIA AND THROMBOCYTOPENIA IN A CASE OF TRYPANOSOMA EVANSI - BABESIA GIBSONI CO-INFECTION IN A CLIENT-OWNED DOG
rationale: Dog with weight loss, splenomegaly, non-regenerative anaemia and thrombocytopenia, B. gibsoni and T. evansi PCR-positive, responded to diminazene, quinapyramine and doxycycline.

title: Babesia vulpes in a dog from Prince Edward Island, Canada.
journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne
rationale: Dog referred with suspected IMHA, confirmed B. vulpes, successfully treated with atovaquone/proguanil and azithromycin.

title: Concurrent Trypanosomosis, Babesiosis and Toxocarosis in a Dog: a Case Report.
rationale: Full text: 6-month-old dog with pale, jaundiced mucosae and emaciation, Trypanosoma, Babesia and Toxocara co-infection, treated with diminazene, doxycycline and supportive drugs; did not respond and died 20 days after presentation.

title: Comparative efficiency of chemotherapeutic drugs in babesiosis of dogs
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; icterus; other: fever, haemoglobinuria, vomiting
rationale: Full text (Ukrainian): 128 dogs with acute babesiosis (fever, pale mucosae, red-brown urine) in two groups treated with diminazene (Azidin-vet) or imidocarb (Imkar-120) plus symptomatic therapy; efficacy 93.15% vs 98.2%, faster recovery and lower mortality with imidocarb.

title: Co-infection with Babesia canis and Borrelia burgdorferi S.L. in a dog from northeastern Romania: a case report
journal: Journal of Applied Life Sciences and Environment
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; other: hyperthermia, inflammatory syndrome; coinfection
rationale: Dog with haemolytic anaemia that became severe, with large Babesia on smear, died during blood transfusion before antibabesial therapy; transfusion was given for babesia-associated anaemia and death is the outcome.

title: Multiple point mutations in cytochrome b gene of Babesia gibsoni - A possible cause for buparvaquone resistance.
rationale: Twelve dogs given buparvaquone-azithromycin; haematology improved, 8 had persistent parasitaemia and were genotyped for cytb mutations. Clinical syndrome only lightly described.

title: EFFICIENCY OF APPLICATION OF THE DRUG "HEPTRAL-VET" IN THE COMPLEX TREATMENT OF DOGS WITH ACUTE COURSE OF PYROPLASMOSIS
journal: Scientific and Technical Bulletin оf State Scientific Research Control Institute of Veterinary Medical Products and Fodder Additives аnd Institute of Animal Biology
rationale: Eight dogs with acute piroplasmosis, anaemia and raised liver enzymes were given ademetionine after specific therapy; haematology and biochemistry improved by day 7.

title: Diagnosis dan Pengobatan Babesiosis pada Anjing Shih-Tzu di Klinik Lilipoet, Yogyakarta, Indonesia
rationale: Shih-Tzu with fever, lethargy, anorexia, vomiting and thrombocytopenia (32 x10^3/uL), PCR-positive; treated with diminazene and doxycycline for 14 days; platelets rose to 75 x10^3/uL and PCR was negative 14 days after treatment (declared cured).

title: Diagnosis of subclinical stage of Babesia gibsoni and its’s therapeutic management in dogs
rationale: Ten dogs with vague signs and normal haematology, some seizures, treated and all recovered.

title: DIAGNOSIS AND THERAPEUTIC MEASURES FOR PYROPLASMOSIS IN DOGS
journal: VESTNIK OF THE BASHKIR STATE AGRARIAN UNIVERSITY
rationale: Reports results of treating dogs with piroplasmosis using complex agents, judged by correction of haematological and biochemical parameters; dogs had laboratory abnormalities and post-treatment values are the outcome. Drugs and numbers not given in the abstract.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF INFUSION THERAPY IN THE TREATMENT OF DOGS WITH PYROPLASMOSIS
rationale: Three groups of 5 dogs with pyroplasmosis given different infusion therapies; Reamberin shortened recovery by 5 days.

title: Comparative characteristics of various methods of treating babesiosis in dogs
rationale: Comparison of 5% and 12% imidocarb in dogs with babesiosis, with efficacy and side effects reported.

title: EFFECTS OF IMIDOPYRAN AND PREDNISONE IN THE TREATMENT OF BABESIOSIOSIS-ASSOCIATED ANEMIA IN DOGS
rationale: Dogs with babesial haemolytic anaemia treated with imidopyran and prednisolone; erythron indices improved.

title: Babesiosis: Current status and future perspectives in Pakistan and chemotherapy used in livestock and pet animals.
treatments: imidocarb; diminazene; atovaquone; buparvaquone; azithromycin; fluids; transfusion; homeopathic
rationale: Multi-species review covering clinical signs and chemotherapy of babesiosis in pet animals including dogs; canine content is generic, so borderline.

title: SUCCESSFUL TREATMENT OF BABESIAGIBSONI INFECTION IN A PUG DOG - A CASE REPORT
rationale: Pug with severe anaemia, thrombocytopenia and icterus treated with pRBC transfusion and antibiotics plus prednisolone; uneventful recovery in two weeks.

title: The effect of transfusion of erythrocyte mass on clinical and haematological indicators of dogs with hemolytic anaemia caused by babesiosis
rationale: Five anaemic dogs transfused; haematological recovery by day 10.

title: DEMODICOSIS WITH TICKS INFESTATION AND BABESIOSIS IN A MIXED DOG
rationale: Dog with demodicosis, ticks and anaemic babesiosis treated with clindamycin among other drugs; improved by days 7-21.

title: THERAPEUTIC MANAGEMENT OF CANINE BABESIOSIS
syndromes: haemolytic anaemia; thrombocytopenia; aki; hepatopathy; icterus
rationale: Labrador with anaemia, thrombocytopenia and raised urea, creatinine and bilirubin treated with triple antibiotics; recovered after 15 days.

title: Canine babesiosis: A report of two different cases
journal: International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
rationale: Two dogs given imidocarb; one recovered and one with oliguria and azotaemia died of acute renal failure.

title: Jaundice in a dog secondary to babesiosis: A case report
journal: International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
rationale: Jaundiced Golden Retriever treated with standard babesiosis drugs plus supportive care; recovery confirmed at 30 days by laboratory tests and ultrasound.

title: Clinico diagnostic and therapeutic management of Babesia gibsoni infection in dogs
